target: मंगलवार और शुक्रवार को बाज़ार में बहुत भीड़ होती है।
english: The market is very crowded on Tuesdays and Fridays.
reason: Advertising/shop-sign register ("विशेष छूट मिलती है"), not everyday speech. Replacement keeps the same days-of-week + habitual present pattern with something a person would actually say.

target: यह आम पिछले वाले से ज़्यादा मीठा है।
english: This mango is sweeter than the last one.
reason: Vacuous textbook trivia — nobody compares the sweetness of carrots and radishes. Replacement keeps the same से ज़्यादा + adjective comparison in a real situation.

target: मेरी भाभी बहुत अच्छी और समझदार हैं।
english: My sister-in-law is very nice and sensible.
reason: "व्यवहारकुशल" is literary/written Hindi that no one uses in conversation, and the praise is padded. Replacement keeps possessive + two adjectives + हैं in ordinary spoken register.

target: शीला ने आज सुबह घर की सफ़ाई की।
english: Sheela cleaned the house this morning.
reason: Name-swap duplicate of hi-0749 ("सविता सुबह जल्दी उठी और योग किया") — padding, and the conjoined clause drops the required ने. Replacement is a clean ने-perfective sentence with different content.

target: मीना ने कल बाज़ार से सब्ज़ी ख़रीदी।
english: Meena bought vegetables from the market yesterday.
reason: "भारत" as a person's name reads as "India bought goods" to a learner, and "सामान ख़रीदा" is vague filler. Replacement keeps the ने-perfective + से pattern with a concrete object.

target: पवन ने कल दोस्तों के साथ फ़िल्म देखी।
english: Pawan watched a movie with friends yesterday.
reason: Word-for-word duplicate of hi-0754 with only the name changed — padding. Replacement keeps the ने-perfective past with everyday vocabulary.

target: रमेश, तुम्हें डॉक्टर को दिखाना चाहिए।
english: Ramesh, you should see a doctor.
reason: Word-for-word duplicate of hi-1001 with only the name changed — padding. Replacement keeps the चाहिए obligation pattern in a different, very common situation.

target: बाज़ार मॉल से ज़्यादा नज़दीक है।
english: The market is closer than the mall.
reason: As written, "बाज़ार मॉल से नज़दीक है" reads as "the market is near the mall", which contradicts the English. Adding ज़्यादा makes it the intended comparative and matches how people actually say it.

target: इस किताब की क़ीमत छह सौ रुपये के क़रीब है।
english: This book costs around six hundred rupees.
reason: Census/officialese trivia — village population is not something a learner will ever say. Replacement keeps the की + number + के क़रीब pattern in a shopping context.

target: दरवाज़ा खोलो, बाहर कोई खड़ा है।
english: Open the door, someone is standing outside.
reason: "किवाड़" is archaic/rural and would never be taught to a beginner; the everyday word is दरवाज़ा. Same imperative, same clause structure.

target: बाज़ार यहाँ से सिर्फ़ आधा किलोमीटर दूर है।
english: The market is only half a kilometer from here.
reason: Compass-direction translationese — no one gives directions in Hindi with "पश्चिम में". Replacement keeps यहाँ से + distance in the way people really say it.
